mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls by >10% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, depressing business investment and consumer confidence, and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE > 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 3% over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by >3% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 0.5 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall of more than 2% in industrial production (INDPRO) within a single month signals a synchronized labor and supply shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.5pp AND INDPRO monthly change < -2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises by >0.5pp and INDPRO falls by >2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a recession signals aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 2% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 2% coincides with UNRATE > 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coincident with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 signals deteriorating labor market conditions, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.4pp AND PAYEMS monthly change < -100000
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises by >0.4pp and PAYEMS falls by >100,000 in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals insufficient demand to support earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during any four-quarter period where GDPC1 < 1% annualized.
